title: The largest element, on two devices
starter:
%x    = buffer 16 dtype=i32 slot=0
%p    = buffer 2 dtype=i32 slot=1
%m    = buffer 1 dtype=i32 slot=2
%acc  = alloc 1 dtype=i32

hints: Start from c_partial_sums above: the same buffers, the same two kernels. Keep its shard size of 8, and change the two adds that combine numbers into max.
%acc starts at 0, so a shard of negative numbers would give 0. In the loop over %k, compute %big = max %cur %xe and %first = cmplt %k 1, then store %new = where %first %xe %big.

After the device loop, %p1 = after %p %ed. The last kernel is %g = range 1 axis=global with %w = range 1 axis=local inside: load p[w] and p[w + 1] through %p1, take their max and store it at m[w + g].

answer.code:
%x    = buffer 16 dtype=i32 slot=0
%p    = buffer 2 dtype=i32 slot=1
%m    = buffer 1 dtype=i32 slot=2
%acc  = alloc 1 dtype=i32
%d    = range 2 axis=device
%b    = range 1 axis=global
%t    = range 1 axis=local
%k    = range 8
%ds   = mul %d 8
%i    = add %ds %k
%xv   = shrink %x %i []
%xe   = load %xv
%tb   = add %t %b
%av   = shrink %acc %tb []
%cur  = load %av
%big  = max %cur %xe
%first = cmplt %k 1
%new  = where %first %xe %big
%st   = store %av %new
%ek   = end %st %k
%et   = end %ek %t
%acc1 = after %acc %et
%u    = range 1 axis=local
%ub   = add %u %b
%rv   = shrink %acc1 %ub []
%res  = load %rv
%po   = add %d %ub
%pv   = shrink %p %po []
%sp   = store %pv %res
%eu   = end %sp %u
%eb   = end %et %eu %b
%ed   = end %eb %d
%p1   = after %p %ed
%g    = range 1 axis=global
%w    = range 1 axis=local
%q0   = shrink %p1 %w []
%a0   = load %q0
%w1   = add %w 1
%q1   = shrink %p1 %w1 []
%a1   = load %q1
%top  = max %a0 %a1
%wg   = add %w %g
%mv   = shrink %m %wg []
%sm   = store %mv %top
%ew   = end %sm %w
%eg   = end %ew %g
%m1   = after %m %eg
answer.explain: Each device runs one kernel that walks its 8 elements, x[8d + k], keeping the largest so far in acc, and stores it at p[d]. At k = 0 the where takes the element itself, because acc starts at 0 and 0 is larger than every negative number. A kernel after the device loop runs on device 0 and stores the larger of p[0] and p[1] in m. Max, like integer add, gives the same answer in any order, so this one would not change with the order.

require: the partial maxima come from a device loop: %d = range 2 axis=device
